title: Engagement slipped 3 points, and nearly all of the drop is in our fulfilment centres
subtitle: The 2026 engagement survey had our highest response rate yet (81%). Corporate engagement held steady. FC engagement fell 4 points, driven by workload and unpredictable schedules, and Dallas fell furthest.
summary: 81% of employees took the 2026 engagement survey, a record. The engagement index fell from 71% to 68% favourable. Corporate was flat, while FCs fell 4 points and Dallas FC fell 8. Manager support, growth and workload are the biggest drivers company-wide, and for FC associates schedule predictability matters most. We recommend acting first on FC scheduling (starting in Dallas) and on internal mobility.
key_findings: Response rate was 81% (2,317 of 2,860), up 4 pp; FC response reached a record 77%.
The engagement index fell 3 points to 68% favourable. Corporate was flat at 74%, FCs fell 4 points to 64%.
Dallas FC fell 8 points to 59% (±4.8), the lowest of any group; its schedule predictability score is 34%.
Manager support, growth and workload explain 62% of the modelled variation in engagement. For FC associates alone, schedule predictability is the top driver (22%).
Workload and staffing (27%) and career paths (21%) are the most common themes across 1,142 written comments.
